It uses only Node.js 26 built-ins (`node:http`, `node:sqlite`, `node:crypto`) and plain JavaScript ES modules.\n\n## Starting and verifying the server\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` runs `node server.js` in the foreground. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` and reads the port from the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `3000`.\n\nVerify it is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n# {\"ok\":true}\n```\n\n## Entry point and major files\n\n- **`server.js`** — Entry point. Creates the HTTP server, wires the route table via `lib/router.js`, resets the SQLite database with `db.resetDb()`, and starts listening. The route table is grouped by domain, with parameterized routes registered before more general parents that could shadow them.\n- **`lib/router.js`** — Minimal HTTP router. Routes are registered with `.get()`, `.post()`, `.put()`, and `.delete()` and matched by HTTP method and regex. Captured path segments are spread as positional arguments to the handler. Bodies are read only for `POST` and `PUT`.\n- **`lib/db.js`** — Persistence layer. Owns the SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection, the schema, and all CRUD operations. Schema creation is centralized in `ensureSchema()` and used by both initialization and reset. This is the only destructive endpoint and is intended for tests. The drop order follows the dependency order in `lib/db.js` so foreign-key constraints are satisfied. The server also calls `db.resetDb()` on startup for a deterministic baseline.\n\n### Request routing\n\n`server.js` builds a `Router` from `lib/router.js`. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. The route table is grouped by domain in `server.js`, but the order within each domain is preserved from previous stages so that parameterized routes (e.g., `/v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`) are still registered before their more general parents (`/v1/combat/sessions`).\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET`, `DELETE`, or any method other than `POST`/`PUT` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` or `PUT` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- `POST` or `PUT` with a matching route reads the body and runs the handler.\n\n`POST`/`PUT` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Handlers parse it with `lib/http.js::parseJson` via `lib/handlers.js::requireBody`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n\n### Module and data-flow boundaries\n\n```\n server.js   ──▶  lib/router.js  ──▶  lib/handlers.js\n                                     │\n                                     ▼\n              ┌─────────────────────┴─────────────┐\n              ▼                                   ▼\n       lib/db.js                            lib/domain.js\n    (SQLite + schema)                      (pure logic)\n              │\n              ▼\n       lib/http.js\n  (responses + body reading)\n```\n\n- `server.js` only routes and starts the server.\n- `lib/router.js` only matches methods/patterns and reads bodies for POST/PUT.\n- `lib/handlers.js` only validates HTTP input, calls the DB/domain layer, and serializes responses. Shared helpers handle repeated authorization, turn checks, and response formatting.\n- `lib/db.js` only talks to SQLite and maps rows to/from JS objects.\n- `lib/domain.js` has no side effects and no knowledge of HTTP or SQLite.\n- `lib/http.js` only provides HTTP utilities and does not depend on the other modules.\n\n## Main API / domain groupings\n\n| Group | Endpoints | Purpose 'dm' : 'player';\n  const nextTurnNumber = campaign.turn_number + turnNumberDelta;\n  return { nextActor, nextPhase, nextTurnNumber, nextIndex };\n}\n\n// Check whether a user is the campaign owner or a joined member. Sends 403\n// and returns null if neither. Otherwise returns { isOwner, isMember }.\nfunction authorizePlayParticipant(res, campaign, user, campaignId) {\n  const isOwner = campaign.owner === user.username;\n  const isMember = db.getPlayMembership(campaignId, user.username) !== null;\n  if (!isOwner && !isMember) {\n    forbidden(res, 'forbidden');\n    return null;\n  }\n  return { isOwner, isMember };\n}\n\n// Load a play campaign and its encounter, enforcing membership and optional\n// encounter constraints. The owner may always advance or delay\n// a turn; the active player combatant may also advance or delay their own\n// turn. Only the active player combatant may ready or submit an action.\nfunction requireEncounterOwnerOrActiveMember(res, user, campaign, order, turnIndex) {\n  const active = order[turnIndex];\n  let allowed = campaign.owner === user.username;\n  if (!allowed && active.member && active.member === user.username) {\n    allowed = true;\n  }\n  if (!allowed) {\n    conflict(res, 'not your turn');\n    return false;\n  }\n  return true;\n}\n\nfunction requireActiveEncounterMember(res, user, order, turnIndex) {\n  const active = order[turnIndex];\n  if (!active.member || active.member !== user.username) {\n    conflict(res, 'not your turn');\n    return false;\n  }\n  return true;\n}\n\n// Resolve a damage/heal target against an encounter roster. sendJson(res, 200, {\n    level,\n    proficiency_bonus: domain.proficiencyBonus(level),\n    hp_max: hpMax,\n    armor_class: armorClass,\n    modifiers,\n  });\n}\n\n// ---------- PHB rules []), encounter.round ?? 1, encounter.turn_index ?? 0);\n}\n\n// Internal helper: add a combatant to an encounter if it is not already\n// present (by the supplied key). Resets the persisted initiative order so the\n// next turn read recomputes from the updated roster.\nfunction addCombatant(campaignId, encounterId, combatant, keyFn) {\n  const encounter = getPlayEncounter(campaignId, encounterId);\n  if (!encounter) return null;\n  const combatants = encounter.combatants ?? [];\n  if (combatants.some(c => keyFn(c) === keyFn(combatant))) {\n    return { duplicate: true };\n  }\n  combatants.push(combatant);\n  const round = encounter.round ?? 1;\n  const turnIndex = encounter.turn_index ?? 0;\n  const stmt = db.prepare('UPDATE play_encounters SET combatants_json = ?, order_json = ?, round = ?, turn_index = ? WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?');\n  stmt.run(JSON.stringify(combatants), '[]', round, turnIndex, campaignId, encounterId);\n  return { combatant };\n}\n\n// Internal helper: remove a combatant from an encounter by key. If the\n// roster becomes empty, reset round/turn; otherwise keep the turn index in\n// bounds.\nfunction removeCombatant(campaignId, encounterId, keyValue, keyFn) {\n  const encounter = getPlayEncounter(campaignId, encounterId);\n  if (!encounter) return null;\n  const combatants = encounter.combatants ?? AND loot_id = ?');\n    const row = stmt.get(campaignId, lootId);\n    if (!row) {\n      db.exec('ROLLBACK');\n      return { notFound: true };\n    }\n    if (row.status !== 'open') {\n      db.exec('ROLLBACK');\n      return { closed: true };\n    }\n    const votes = parseJson(row.votes_json, []);\n    if (votes.some(v => v.voter === voter)) {\n      db.exec('ROLLBACK');\n      return { alreadyVoted: true };\n    }\n    votes.push({ voter, recipient_character_id: recipient });\n    const update = db.prepare('UPDATE play_loot SET votes_json = ? AND loot_id = ?');\n    const row = stmt.get(campaignId, lootId);\n    if (!row) {\n      db.exec('ROLLBACK');\n      return { notFound: true };\n    }\n    if (row.status !== 'open') {\n      db.exec('ROLLBACK');\n      return { alreadyAssigned: true };\n    }\n    addPlayCharacterInventoryItem(campaignId, recipientCharacterId, row.item_id, row.quantity);\n    const update = db.prepare(\"UPDATE play_loot SET status = 'assigned', recipient_character_id = ?
